newsitem.title: USA: Farmland says HRW damage estimates ongoing effort.
newsitem.headline: Farmland says HRW damage estimates ongoing effort.

text.p: A freeze damage estimate for the U.S. hard red winter wheat crop attributed to Farmland Industries this week was described as part of an ongoing effort to track wheat market trends, a company statement said.

"Our assessment of the HRW wheat crop is ongoing and will continue until harvest, with our experts doing survey work in the field," John F. Berardi, executive vice president with Farmland in Kansas City, Mo, said in the statement.
Wire services Thursday reported Farmland estimated freeze damage to the winter wheat crop at not more than 117 million bushels. Farmland declined comment on that figure on Friday.
"Farmland continues to believe that the high estimates of of damaged crop were overstated," the Berardi statement said.
Officials at Farmland and its Grain Division, a leading wheat exporter, declined further comment on the assessment.
"They (Farmland traders) do this every day, but they don't release it publicly," a Farmland spokeswoman said.
Wheat prices fell Thursday as talk of the assessment circulated, since that number was much lower than previous damage estimates from other agronomists and grain traders.
Some early damage estimates for Kansas alone had reached the 100 million bushel mark after the April 12-13 hard freeze hit wheat crops in Texas, Oklahoma and Kansas.
